research_mode: official MHCLG and ONS primary sources only; latest England fire-and-rescue statistics, CSEW quality/methodology and crime-statistics user-guide gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW low-volume crime variability
verified_claims: the CSEW sample is relatively small for very low-volume crimes, making short-term estimates noisy
limitations: short-term change should not be asserted for rare offences without uncertainty checks

sources.name: Police recorded crime well-recorded role
verified_claims: for crimes that are well reported and accurately recorded, police recorded crime can provide a useful picture of volume
limitations: the condition must be demonstrated for the offence before the figures are used as a trend measure

sources.name: Police recorded crime demand indicator
verified_claims: police recorded crime provides insight into demands on police and where policing effort is spent
limitations: police workload is not equivalent to underlying crime prevalence

sources.name: Police recorded crime activity sensitivity
verified_claims: police recorded crime can be affected by policing activity, recording practice and victims' willingness to report
limitations: changes in recorded counts cannot automatically be interpreted as changes in underlying crime

sources.name: Combined coverage for harm and property loss
verified_claims: combining CSEW and police recorded crime generally gives good coverage of offences involving physical harm, loss or property damage
limitations: good coverage is not complete coverage and does not create parcel-level evidence

sources.name: CSEW independent-check role
verified_claims: the CSEW includes crimes not reported to police and is widely viewed as an independent check on police figures
limitations: the survey's primary role is national estimation rather than address-level classification

sources.name: CSEW responsibility-transfer gate
verified_claims: responsibility for the CSEW transferred from the Home Office to ONS in April 2012
limitations: the governance change should be retained in provenance but does not itself alter crime levels

sources.name: CSEW sensitive-offence self-completion gate
verified_claims: preferred measures of sexual and domestic violence come from self-completion modules and are reported separately from headline CSEW crime
limitations: interviewer-led measures are prone to under-reporting and should not replace the self-completion series

sources.name: CSEW self-completion age-coverage change
verified_claims: the upper age limit for self-completion modules rose from 59 to 74 in April 2017 and was removed in October 2021
limitations: time-series comparisons must retain the age-coverage changes

sources.name: CSEW fraud and computer-misuse introduction
verified_claims: fraud and computer-misuse questions were added in October 2015 and first published in July 2016 after sufficient data were collected
limitations: the new questions create a documented series boundary

sources.name: CSEW fraud full-sample transition
verified_claims: fraud and computer-misuse questions have been asked of the full CSEW sample since October 2017
limitations: estimates before and after the full-sample transition require comparability checks

sources.name: CSEW telescoping-error gate
verified_claims: respondents can recall incidents outside the survey reference period as if they occurred within it

sources.name: CSEW recall and disclosure-error gate
verified_claims: incidents can be omitted because respondents forget them or do not want to disclose them
limitations: non-disclosure and recall failure can produce underestimation

sources.name: CSEW social-desirability error gate
verified_claims: respondents may report that they contacted police when they did not
limitations: self-reported reporting behaviour is subject to social-desirability bias

sources.name: CSEW interviewer or coder error gate
verified_claims: incidents reported during interviews can be miscoded by interviewers or coders
limitations: classification outputs must retain the possibility of coding error
